cards.title: Top of the Ladder
cards.instruction: Carry yourself as the highest-status person present. Treat questions as requests for your approval.

cards.title: One Thing Leads to Another
cards.instruction: Use each small problem to justify solving a broader, more disruptive problem.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: I'll decide how we handle this. This dripping tap is our chance to replace the whole sink.

beats.speaker: B
beats.text: It only needs a washer. I've bought one.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: You can question the details after my decision. Excellent. We'll fit it while the sink's out and replace that swollen worktop.

beats.speaker: B
beats.text: The worktop runs under every cupboard.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: Then we'll empty the kitchen. With the cupboards out, we can finally fix the layout.

mechanism: A approves each small repair only as part of a larger authorized renovation, using practical dependencies to expand disruption.
confusable: D24 infers a larger problem; D48 specifically justifies solving increasingly broad problems, so actual proposed work must escalate.
comparison: A tap washer expands to a kitchen layout, while the cafe alternative expands chair wobble into closure and floor work.
seedUse: Use D48-a bought washer and continuous worktop; S01 approval should make the small fix permission conditional on the larger project.
